title: The lane lint "unknown" line on a ready PR names the return-to-draft remedy, and the lane brief template carries the rule
why: Debt named by runner 10 (08:02 CST Nov 14, relayed): a ready PR that goes red and gets a lane push must return to draft first. Sightings: #3272 (ready run red in checks-mutate-guard, test_guard_beat.py line 307; made draft again by hand, lane fixing) and #3238 (lane lint unknown on a ready head). Coordinator read of main 60db33f8801c merge/merge.py by grep, 08:04 (not the whole file; triage read none): (a) stale_page_remedy (about line 3137) prints "Return #N to draft ... run merge N --confirm on the draft ... then mark ready" and DRAFT_ROUTES (about line 1952) names the two routes, but only for a stale records page on a ready PR. (b) draft_run_state (about lines 1297-1319) reads a ready head's skipped `touched` job as "unknown ... no touched test ran", which is what runner 10 hit on #3238 and #3272's lane lint; it prints the symptom, not the remedy. (c) No step converts a PR to draft or refuses a lane push onto a ready red PR; runner 10 toggled both by hand. Scope after the coordinator's read (rewritten 08:08 CST Nov 14, replacing triage's two-candidate list): (1) make the lane-lint "unknown" line name the return-to-draft remedy, reusing DRAFT_ROUTES (one home); (2) put the rule in the lane brief template. Not read by the coordinator: the tool's phase code, or whether the cloud route has failed anywhere. A message change to a check's output; no verdict changes, so round 3 does not apply by itself. Red first: a ready head with a skipped touched job prints the remedy line; a draft head does not.
note: Filed 08:06 CST Nov 14 by triage. Tracker: the coordinator. No lane yet.
